newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Alcatel unveils ambitious plans for Thomson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Alcatel unveils ambitious plans for Thomson.

text.p: France's Alcatel Alsthom SA on Wednesday unveiled plans to build state-owned consumer and defence electronics group Thomson SA into the world's number two defence supplier and a big consumer group.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk told a news conference he had submitted the Alcatel's offer to acquire Thomson to the government on Monday and, after months of silence, he unveiled Alcatel's ambitions if it won the contest.
The sole other bidder for Thomson, Lagardere Groupe, has waged a very public campaign to obtain the favour of the government.
Tchuruk said Alcatel wanted to acquire Thomson SA as a whole, which means the profitable 58-percent Thomson-CSF as well as the loss-making Thomson Multimedia consumer electronics group.
The Alcatel chairman said he planned to buy-out the minority shareholders in Thomson-CSF and take the group off the Bourse.

He said that Alcatel would seek a "wide scale partnership with another major industrial player of the (defence) sector" to hoist Thomson-CSF to the rank of the world's number two defence group, overtaking GM Hughes Electronics Corp but staying behind Lockheed Martin.

Tchuruk confided to reporters that it would be "logical" Alcatel studied such a partnership with Britain's GEC Plc, its joint-venture partner in the GEC-Alsthom industrial power and high speed train company.
But he did not exclude others and said he prefered to keep his options open.
Lagardere has named British Aerospace Plc and Daimler-Benz's DASA as potential partners if it wins the beauty contest.
Tchuruk said that a combination of Alcatel's and Thomson-CSF's technologies would make a leader in defence communication networks which are becoming more and more important in modern warfare.

For Thomson Multimedia, already the number one television company in the U.S. with the RCA and General Electric brands and number two in Europe behind Philips Industries, Thuruck also had big ambitions.
In the world consumer electronics market, Thomson Multimedia ranks fourth behind Sony Corp and Mitsubishi Corp of Japan and Philips.
Firstly he noted that the increasing digitalisation of products was creating new markets by linking consumer electronics with communications networks.

Secondly he said that the group would need to restructure its "old" business of television sets and video recorders -- reducing the number of its brands in Europe from six and cutting costs -- and forge ahead in the digital world, building on its leading position in decoders.

Tchuruk said he would look for an Asian partner to bring both market access to the southeast Asian countries as expertise in efficient production. He declined to speculate on a name and also made no comment on rumours the Asian partner could take up to 35 percent in Thomson Multimedia.

Tchuruk also kept quiet about the financial details of the offer. Newspapers have suggested that the government may have to pump between five and eight billion francs ($1.56 billion) into Thomson SA prior to the sale.

"It is up to the government to decide whether a capital increase is needed," Tchuruk said. But he nevertheless made it clear that he did not want the Thomson acquisition to increase the Alcatel Alsthom debt-to-equity ratio of 30 percent.
